owner_ruling: 2026-10-15 daily development server three-database build; no formal production release and no production topology change

demo_seed.reason: The owner ruling of 2026-10-16 declares smart_construction_demo the demo duty's data carrier: demo data is produced by the product's own formal demo seed chain, never by a substitute fixture lane and never by writing a terminal state directly. The chain has the two stages the product's own full-demo loader has -- the release scenario set, then the declared profile -- because the profile's payment step resolves an S69 contract xmlid that only the scenario set creates; a declared stage list without the release set would seed a partial carrier. The product tree names the carrier, the stages and the profile; the governed demo-seed entry reads this section instead of defaulting a step list of its own, and the seed's own guard still has to accept the database, the environment and the explicit demo-data switch before anything runs.

duties.acceptance_fixture_policy: The demo duty is the standard platform tenant users evaluate, so it carries only the product demo data chain. The deterministic acceptance fixture (FE Company A/B and the fixture identities) belongs to a dedicated acceptance carrier, not to this tenant; declaring no acceptance_fixture here keeps a future rebuild from reinstalling test identities into the demo database. The fixture module and its isolated acceptance lane remain intact.

protected_historic_sources.reason: Before the 2026-10-16 rebuild, the demo duty borrowed this pre-governance cluster, and it also carries a company-1 tenant volume. The owner ruling keeps it unchanged in place: no rename, no clean, no migration, no upgrade and no seed. It is registered here for one reason -- a database *name* must stop identifying a target on its own. Once the rebuilt demo carrier also carries a database named sc_demo, a bare database name resolves to two carriers, and any governed entry that receives only a name has to refuse instead of guessing which one is meant. This entry declares no duty, so it can never be selected as a write target by the duty entry.

platform_admin_database_note: Single authority for the platform-admin binding. Every duty entry reads the deployed frontend build environment back from frontend_build_env_file and refuses when it names another database, so the declaration, the deployed runtime and the repository guards cannot drift into two dialects.
edition_release_note: Verified meaning of smart_core.platform_release_db on this server: it names the database that *carries* the effective release snapshot of the runtime that runs there, not a platform-wide publication authority. The production acceptance clone runtime rebinds a restored copy to itself, and the daily platform-control duty holds neither the parameter nor any snapshot row, so a duty that declares edition.carrier=effective_release_snapshot may publish a declared edition into itself while holding no platform publication right. Each duty may only publish its own edition.allowed_product_keys, and preview is never widened automatically. The platform-control duty declares no edition and is refused by the entry.

managed_duty_instances.note: The product tree carries the generic duties only. A duty whose data_purpose is customer is supplied by the managed instance document under ops_root, written 0600 outside the git checkout by the governed entry. Resolution merges the two and refuses when a required instance is missing or unreadable, still carries a placeholder, breaks the naming rules, or disagrees with the duty it claims to be.
